# Meal Monster

> Meal Monster is an iPhone food tracker for adults. Users log food by describing it in natural text, by voice, with a food photo, or by scanning a supported packaged-food barcode. The app creates an editable estimate of calories, protein, carbohydrates and fat, tracks daily totals, and shows progress against calorie and macro targets over Day, Week, Month, six-month and Year views.

## Key facts
- Platform: iPhone (iOS). App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6787743894
- Logging: natural-language text or voice for one food or a whole meal (e.g. "chicken, rice and a salad"); food photos (estimates what is visible, cannot guarantee every ingredient or portion); supported barcodes (coverage varies).
- Estimates are editable (food details, servings, calories, macros) and Undo is available. They are estimates, not exact measurements.
- Goals: Lose weight, Gain weight, Maintain my weight, or Eat healthier. Starting targets are estimated from goal, body and activity inputs and can be adjusted. Targets are not a meal plan or medical prescription.
- AI: meal text, voice and photos are sent to OpenAI only after affirmative, revocable AI data consent. AI usage limits apply.
- Apple Health: optional, read-only (steps and workout/activity). Meal Monster does not write to Apple Health.
- Friends: per-friend, revocable sharing of today's calories, base daily goal, display name, equipped skin and logging streak only. Friends never see meals, food names, macros, weight, workouts or health data. Not a social feed or chat.
- Pricing: food tracking is part of Meal Monster Pro (subscription); a free Supporter mode exists for trusted friends. Current prices and any trial are shown in the App Store.
- Not medical advice, a diagnosis tool, or eating-disorder treatment. For adults.
- Character: Meal Monster is a companion mascot; collectible skins are earned through consistent logging, never sold individually.

## Research (original data studies)
- [What 1,000 Weight Loss Transformations Have in Common](https://mealmonster.app/research/weight-loss-transformations/): top 1,000 YouTube weight loss stories (296 h). 48% combined one way of eating with one way of moving; tracking food was the #1 eating change (25%); median 3 methods; 93% used neither GLP-1 medication nor surgery; people who had failed before were 1.7x more likely to use a fasting window and to meal prep.
- [What People Who Lost Weight Wish They Knew Sooner](https://mealmonster.app/research/what-people-wish-they-knew/): 300 first-person stories. Most repeated lesson: calories matter, but you don't have to count every single one.
